title: All About Beetles
checkpoint: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about beetles.
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about beetles.

pages.text: A bug sits on a log.
pages.illustration: A shiny black beetle resting on top of a mossy log in a log pile.

pages.text: A bug has a hard shell on top.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the beetle showing its hard, glossy black wing case on its back.
A clear view of the beetle from above, its six legs visible underneath it.

pages.text: A bug can tuck its legs in.
pages.illustration: The beetle with its legs pulled in close to its body, tucked tight.

pages.text: A bug hides under the bark.
pages.illustration: The beetle crawling under a loose flap of bark on the log.

pages.text: A bug can lift bits of wood.
pages.illustration: The beetle pushing against a small piece of soft, rotten wood.

pages.text: A bug digs in the soft wood.
pages.illustration: The beetle burrowing into the soft, crumbly wood of the old log.

pages.text: Ned spots a bug on the log pile.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling leaning in to look closely at the beetle on the log pile.

pages.text: Ned looks at the hard shell.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling examining the glossy black shell of the beetle up close.

pages.text: Bugs are fun to spot in the log pile.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling smiling, the beetle resting calmly on the log beside him.
